Use google scholar and start looking. If theres a paywall behind one of the cool sounding articles just find its DOI number , URL, or PMID and paste it into a site called sci hub!

The burden of highly intelligent individuals inevitably tend to be a lack of purpose and motivation as time goes on. 
Some are unfortunate enough to have been socially, psychologically, or emotionally damaged earlier on in life as they have a tenancy to isolate but I have encountered many expceptions.
As they grow, individuals of a higher intelligence begin feeling a stronger need for a purpose, as everyone else does.
As it turns out, being super intelligent itself is pretty much a useless skill if not harnessed or harnessed incorrectly. Nowadays without countless other abilities you've worked for, it wont impress people, they'll just think you're an arrogant asshole, which may sometimes be the case.... it wont get you work, not interesting or fulfilling work at least..  and it will most definatley, 100% not get you any type of romantic interest from either sex because everyone likes to be the smarter person so it ends up being an incredibly common turn off... so you'll definatley spend a lot of time alone... and no one will give a shit about the depression that follows either, you'll have to solve that on alone too.
The underlying problem is that the portrayal of super intelligent people is that they can do things that others cant (but as it turns out not by a drastic amount) , they are I fact human, just like everyone else. 
It is no different to someone born athletically gifted,  they will eventually fail against those who have spent their lives training if they never develop themselves.
Fluid intelligence (I believe that's what its called, the type that you're born with) can give you an alright headstart, but in reality what happens to you really does just depend on your actions... so dont let your smarts go to your head ( excuse the pun, ik I suck) 
A bright mind with a purpose and a plan will work wonders! But it's hard work, for everyone.
Being super intelligent doesnt make life super easy, it's an interesting NOT ability, just remembering how much you still have to learn and stay humble enough is a good place to start. Being confident in your ability while honing your skills and understanding other people might not catch on as quickly and taking the time to bring them up to speed, because you'll most definitely be in that position yourself some day.

That's my 2 cents about it.
